title: Bringing a serving stack up on new silicon
subtitle: Patching Intel's Xe2 kernel stack where it had gaps, with outputs that stayed identical

stats.label: special-value combinations checked in one exact, flat rewrite
attention candidates rejected and kept as negatives
memory fences added for a synchronisation the original lacked

lede: The Intel Arc Pro GPU is a new architecture, and the open kernel stacks that serve large models on it had gaps when I started: a GEMM path that chose the wrong tile for prefill, a recurrent-layer prefill with poor occupancy and a missing synchronisation, a missing attention statistic my memory layer needs, and run-to-run variance in some GEMM shapes. I patched the vendor's own sources inside the vendor's toolchain, with an identical-output gate on every change. Outputs stayed unchanged on the gated path. Serving on brand-new hardware means working above a kernel stack that is still catching up with the silicon.
quote: Exactness is a property I want in the product.
evidence: Intel GPU and SYCL/oneAPI engineering: patched the vendor's open kernel stacks on Intel Xe2 hardware to cut cold 32K-token prefill from 21.54 s to 17.23 s with identical outputs.
GPU kernel development: a recurrent-layer prefill fix for occupancy, output split and a missing synchronisation, with 5 memory fences added.
Numerical reproducibility and bitwise validation: an exact kernel rewrite checked across 48 special-value combinations, kept for exactness with no whole-workload gain.
Performance engineering discipline: one change, one patch, one gate, with 2 attention candidates rejected and kept as documented negatives.
author: Corey James
